etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English assemblen, from Old French assembler (“to assemble”), from Medieval Latin assimulāre (“to bring together”), from ad- +‎ simulō (“copy, imitate”), from similis (“like, similar”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“together, one”). Doublet of assimilate.

quote.citation: 1918, The Industrial Education Survey of the City of New York, page 44:
quote.text: The handman reads copy and assembles type by hand, including straight composition, tables and display.

quote.citation: 2019 March 6, Alexis C. Madrigal, “The Servant Economy”, in The Atlantic‎[1]:
quote.text: This micro-generation of Silicon Valley start-ups did two basic things: It put together a labor pool to deliver food or clean toilets or assemble IKEA bookshelves, and it found people who needed those things done.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To gather as a group.
